newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Pertamina says oil investment rules adequate.
newsitem.headline: Pertamina says oil investment rules adequate.

text.p: Indonesia's state oil company Pertamina said on Friday the country's current oil investment rules were adequate and it was not considering new incentives for exploration.

"The current oil rules are adequate. There are many investors applying for production sharing contracts under current rules. Why should we provide further incentives," a Pertamina official dealing with oil contractors told Reuters.
Pertamina President-Director Faisal Abda'oe said on Wednesday the current climate was still conducive for oil investment.
"In the last three years we have signed 51 oil contracts, including production sharing contracts and technical assistance contracts," the official said.
"Pertamina is currently negotiating about nine oil contracts," he added without giving details.
Indonesia's Mines and Energy Minister Ida Bagus Sudjana on Wednesday asked the director general of oil and gas, Soepraptono Soelaeman, and Pertamina to study current oil regulations.

"I hope the director general of oil and gas and Pertamina will study whether existing incentives in place since 1994 are enough or need to be revised, and to what extent existing incentives are attracting investors," Sudjana said.

The central plank of the incentives published in 1994 was an increase to 35 percent from 20 percent in the amount of oil to which contractors working in frontier zones under Pertamina's umbrella were entitled.
